chunks: By his chain, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Murazam ibn Hakim, who said:

I accompanied Muhammad ibn Musadif. So when we entered Medina, I fell ill. So he used to go to the Masjid and leave me alone. So I complained of that to Musadif, and he informed Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) with it. So he (peace be upon him) sent a message to him: 'Your sitting with him is superior to your Salat in the Masjid.'
ai.seo_question: Is staying with a sick person better than praying in the mosque?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) prioritizes the social duty of *ziyarah* (visiting the sick) and companionship over the ritual merit of congregational prayer, illustrating the Shia principle that maintaining kinship and social bonds (*silat al-rahim*) holds significant spiritual weight. This reflects the broader jurisprudential view that specific obligations to others can supersede general acts of worship when they prevent neglect of a companion's needs, highlighting the balance between individual piety and communal care in Shia ethics.
